steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Line a 10x15-inch jellyroll pan with parchment paper. Whip cream, 1/2 cup confectioners' sugar, 1/2 cup cocoa, and 1 teaspoon vanilla in a large bowl until thick and stiff. Refrigerate.
Use an electric mixer to beat egg yolks with 1/2 cup sugar in a large bowl, until pale in color, light, and frothy. Blend in 1/3 cup cocoa, 1 ½ teaspoons vanilla, and salt.
Using clean beaters, whip egg whites in a large glass bowl until they form soft peaks. Gradually add 1/4 cup sugar, and beat until whites form stiff peaks.
Immediately fold yolk mixture into whipped egg whites.
Spread the batter evenly into the prepared pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until cake springs back when lightly touched, about 10 to 12 minutes.
Dust a clean dishtowel with confectioners' sugar. Run a knife around the edge of the pan, and turn the warm cake out onto the towel. Remove and discard parchment paper.
Starting at the short edge of the cake, roll the cake up with the towel. Cool for 30 minutes.
Unroll cake, and spread filling to within 1 inch of the edge.
Roll cake up with filling inside. Place seam-side down onto a serving plate, and refrigerate until serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Bûche de Noël
raw_recipe.description: Bûche de Noël is a jelly-roll style chocolate cake with chocolate cream that's decorated to look like a yule log for an incredibly delicious Christmas dessert!

video.description: Are you in need of a show-stopping dessert centerpiece for your holiday table? Let us introduce you to the bûche de Noël. In this video, Nicole shows you how to bake the festive sponge cake that is typically served around Christmastime and is made to look like the seasonal yule log. The yule log represents the new year to come and is said to bring good luck. Make your holidays luckier and sweeter with a slice of the chocolatey buche de Noel.

review.reviewBody: I made this for my daughter's French class Christmas fete. Yes it is alot of work but worth it. I followed other tips like beating the egg yolks a good 5 minutes, greasing the parchment paper very well and I put quite a bit of powdered sugar on the dish towel before rolling. I had enough of the mousse left over to decorate. Here's what I did and it was beautiful (will post a photo later). I cut one end of the log (about 4") at an angle. Frost the sides, top and bottom and use some mousse to "glue" on the stump (piece cut off earlier) then frost the stump as well except for the top. Next run fork tines across the log and upward on the stump so you have ridges like a log. Then dust with powdered sugar and decorate with holly or mistletoe or pine sprigs. I also made mushrooms from chocate truffles stuck onto a piece of broken candy cane rubbed with chocolate, and dipped in powdered sugar.

This cake received applause at our Christmas dinner. And, it should have. After all, my mother and I had to make it twice. Let me explain. You MUST BEAT the egg yolks and sugar until they are very pale. For all of you Texas Aggies out there, BTHO the egg yolks. Let the electric mixer run at the highest speed for at least 5 minutes. Because this cake contains no rising agents like baking powder or yeast, its "fluffy-ness" depends upon the amount of air that you "BEAT" into it - hence the stiff egg whites and the pulverized egg yolks. 

We decorated the cake with whipping cream and homemade mushrooms (hershey kisses and small marshmallows on toothpicks - with red gel polka dots).

The cake is fabulous - as others have said, just make sure to beat the heck out of the yolks! I used the top setting on my mixer for 5-6 minutes. The cake needs the loft that extra air will give. The baking timing is right on - don't leave it in too long. Wrapping in a silicone sheet, then carefully scraping along the back with a spatula when unrolling it, was key. Used the ganache recipe from this site for filling and frosting, then a very cool technique for the bark: spread a thin layer of melted chocolate over a piece of parchment paper, roll it up tightly (doesn't matter what direction), refrigerate til solid, then unroll. The chocolate will break into shards. Work quickly adding it to the ganache frosting - your finger temp will melt the chocolate. Then meringue mushrooms were added. The marzipan snail is my daughter's fabulous addition. 
I'll never use another cake recipe for our buche. This is great!!

I had to make this cake twice because there are some steps NOT listed in the recipe. One, you need to beat the egg YOLKS with sugar for about 5 minutes on high. They need to be very light, pale yellow in color and they need to have air incorporated into them before you add the cocoa ,vanilla and salt. And fold in a small amount at a time into the egg whites, do not dump it in all at once. It takes a bit longer but you decrease the risk of deflating the batter. The other step that is a bit crucial to this recipe is that you need to let the cake cool, on the parchment lined pan, for about 2 minutes before turning it onto the confectioner dusted towel. Then, once you flip it onto the towel, you need to cool it for another minute or two before removing the parchment paper. Also, when removing the parchment, rip it in the center and work peel outwards. It helps keep the ends from sticking to the paper. Don't roll it tightly. Roll it loosely. The hot cake is still settling so if you roll it too tight you risk flattening it. I had to make this recipe twice because, the first time, just following the instructions, it deflated, the paper stuck to the cake and to the towel. The second time, I used my judgement, knowing the cake would stay warm enough for an extended period of time to allow it to cool in the pan before flipping onto the towel and again on the towel before removing the parchment. I think cocoa powder dusted on the parchment before baking might help too. The flavor is nice. For the outer frosting I used a simple buttercream that is just butter, confectioners sugar, cocoa, vanilla and heavy whipping cream. The secret to a good buttercream that holds it's shape is room temperature, soft butter that is whipped using a paddle attachment, NOT a whisk attachment, on high for about 7 minutes, regardless of the recipe ingredients or amounts used.

First time making this cake was a practice run for Christmas this year - so very pleased with it! I followed all the recommendations from previous reviewers which were excellent - the ingredients are fine as is - just tips for the process. Instead of using parchment paper, I used a silicone baking mat (I did spray it with nonstick spray just to be safe) - worked great!! I also used a silicone baking mat instead of the towel, which also worked great. I followed the recommendations for beating the egg yolks for 5 minutes, ensuring the egg whites are properly beat, also waited 10 minutes to turn out the cake onto the towel/mat. I was able to easily reserve some frosting to frost the cake top, I used a fork to make marks resembling tree bark, and I melted a block of semi-sweet chocolate in the oven, spread it thin, then refrigerated so that I could break into pieces of "bark." My practice run cake ended up looking amazing. I recommend holding off on frosting the outside until ready to decorate and serve. It also DOES taste better the 2nd day as another reviewer commented, so very easy to prepare in advance, refrigerate, and then decorate/serve the next day. I had several people taste the cake - they loved it!

Love this recipe! It was so easy that I ended up making two! One for my family and one for my in-laws. Everyone said I put in way too much work. For the "bark" I melted some chocolate chips and then placed it on wax paper and rolled it around my rolling pin until it hardened. When I unrolled it they crumbled off into a nice bark which I scored with a toothpick. I also made mushrooms out of fondant and dipped them in cocoa powder for "dirt" The cakes came out beautiful and I plan on making them every year now.

A great recipe! I made it exactly as it directed me to and the outcome was superb! I added some chocolate bark look on top by melting chocolate chips and spreading thin on wax paper- freezing- then pasting on the top with a little filling.

My 9-year old daughter and I - neither of us very experienced bakers - made this over the holidays and were quite pleased with the final result! We followed the video and the written directions and found it pretty straightforward. We made one modification - we added fine coconut and mini chocolate chips to the mousse-like filling - made it extra yummy and gave it a bit more texture. Coming out of the oven, the cake did stick to the parchment paper, resulting in some severe cracks in the roll. Not sure what we should have done differently. We did put a bit of shortening on the parchment paper to avoid just that, but were sadly unsuccessful. We decided to put some melted chocolate to cover up the mess - and I think it actually turned out even better! (We just melted chocolate chips with a bit of shortening.) It created a super tasty shell over the cake, giving it a more log-like appearance. We had a distanced gathering with neighbors in the backyard to share our creation and it was an all-round huge hit! will definitely try this again!

This is my first Buche de Noel and I am new to baking - it turned out AMAZING! I feel so accomplished as I was so intimidated but I followed the instructions and it was completely doable. I took the advice from others and beat the eggs for 5 minutes. I carved mushrooms out of large marshmallows with a pairing knife and dusted them with cinnamon, they look so real. I made the ganache in the recipe but haven’t decorated it yet as the log looks so real unfrosted. All the elements taste so great, too!

I was thrilled with how this turned out, although it wasn't how I expected. As you can see the cake was very thin. My oven runs hot, so I took it out after 10 minutes but it may have been slightly under, which might be why it collapsed so much. Fortunately, I used all the filling, which made it turn out big enough. Other reviews say there is plenty of filling to do the outside, but I think you need to use it all inside. I followed the directions, including reviewer suggestions to beat the yolks for 5+ minutes. I melted some chocolate chips with cream to very loosely paint the outside to create the bark look. It was light and delicious and I would definitely make it again as it looked fantastic!

I only used a quarter of a cup of cocoa in the whipped cream and it worked great. Save about 1/4 the cream filling for the “frosting” on the outside . Also I saved a big step by just using the parchment to roll it up. I had brushed melted butter on the pan and then on the parchment. I left the cake in the pan to cool for about 20 minutes then rolled it and let it sit for about an hour. I then unrolled it, filled it, and rolled it up again right off the parchment. A few chocolate shavings and icing sugar and it was done.

Our tweaks: 1) Cranberry-raspberry sauce on the side, made of one Ocean Spray Cranberry sauce can and 2 small packs of fresh raspberries (can add a bit sugar if needed), which we boiled for ten minutes, then pressed through sifter 2) 1 pack of Ghirardelli 72% dark baking chocolate was melted and laid on the parchment sheet, and when it was starting to cool, I traced it with finger to make it more bark-like, and then when it was totally cooled down, we broke it to pieces 3) mushrooms were made of big marshmallow puffs cut into two, and small puffs; and plus some cocoa powder underneath I gotta say, the dough took forever, so I'd streamline it. If you're gluten free and want to go through the hassle of flourless chocolate cake, it's worth it, but otherwise next time I will just plan to mix eggs and egg whites together, 6 of them, plus cocoa mixed with sugar, which will need to be blended into stiff peaks, with 6 tablespoons of flour stirred in (not whipped) before baking. Maybe it will be a miserable fail but I'll try to save time :)

Never tried something like this before but I sure liked the way looked and it sounded good too. The recipe was straight forward and the YouTube video certainly helped also. After completion, my Yule Log looked great and, after serving, tasted really good as well. Definitely chocolaty but not overpowering. The filling is so nice and light, everyone commented on it. This is definitely making itself a spot in the Christmas recipe traditions’ book.
First time made it and It came out really good. Thanks to other reviewers hints

I would give it 5 starts not for the discrepancy between instruction and Vedic. One said baked for 10-12 minutes but in Vedic its12-15 minutes. Next time I will know to check cake by touch it . Overall a great recipe.

We make this recipe right here every year! But not for xmas- for my now-about-to-turn-10-yr-old's birthday, which is at the end of December. He says (and I agree) it's the best cake ever. The meringue mushrooms are equally anticipated. And our gluten free friends can partake with no concern. Every year I think perhaps this is the year I add bark frosting. Or outer skin of some sort. Every year I end up with just a good dusting of powdered sugar, a bunch of meringue critters/accents, occasionally sugared cranberries or currants, and it's perfect. Love this one all the way.

Delicious! This was the perfect ending for our Christmas dinner. Deep chocolate flavor and not overly sweet. I decorated it with chocolate bark, meringue mushrooms, sugared cranberry and sugared rosemary sprigs.
not sure what/how happened. my cakewas very thin and broke up. fortunately, the filling held it together.

I make this every year for our daughter, as a tribute to my aunt who used to make it for me. We add sifted instant coffee granules for a mocha coffee flavor. Delicious! It's always a hit and never any leftovers!
Couldn't be more pleased with how this turned out. Even my husband was mildly impressed. Believe in yourself, you are the exception.
